title: Houthi attacks may change energy markets situation: S&P Global Ratings
summary:

title: Uzbekistan textile output up 15.4% YoY in Jan-May 2026

title: Turkish central bank keeps policy rate unchanged at 37%
summary:
Turkiye’s central bank’s monetary policy committee recently kept its policy rate unchanged at 37 per cent, continuing its monetary policy pause for a fourth meeting in a row.

A UNCTAD report has noted strong but increasingly uneven expansion of global trade in H1 2026, with goods trade being worth $13.7 trillion—up by 12.5 per cent YoY. 
A large share of the rise reflects higher prices rather than stronger trade volumes. 
Trade growth may stay positive but more uneven, with gains in selected sectors and regions offset by geopolitical tensions, policy uncertainty and trade costs.

title: Italy replaces Germany as top market for French industrial textiles
summary:
France's industrial textile exports rose 4.9 per cent YoY to $145.80 million in Q1 2026, with Italy overtaking Germany as the largest export market.
Imports also increased 4.7 per cent to $156.61 million, led by Germany and Italy, leaving France a net importer.
The data indicate a diversification of export destinations amid softer German demand.

title: Canada leaders discuss US trade, energy and supply chain priorities
summary:
Canada’s First Ministers met in Charlottetown to discuss Canada-US trade relations, energy security, labour mobility and internal trade barriers. 
Leaders reaffirmed a united approach to addressing US tariff actions, while supporting trade diversification and economic partnerships. 
They also outlined plans to expand electricity infrastructure, strengthen workforce mobility.

title: Australia’s Q2 2026 GDP outlook softens but risks stabilise
summary:
Australia’s economy appears to be stabilising after a period of weakness, but growth remains below potential.
Westpac’s latest nowcast points to 0.2 per cent GDP growth in Q2 2026, with downside risks easing. 
The outlook suggests a gradual recovery, though external shocks, inflation pressures and monetary policy decisions remain key factors shaping business confidence and activity.

title: US envoy says EU actions create trade uncertainty
summary:
Ambassador Greer said European Commission actions against Google and a state-backed Airbus loan are creating uncertainty in the Turnberry Agreement.
He said the moves risk stability and predictability in transatlantic trade and create uncertainty for US exports of goods and services to Europe.
The statement is a policy signal for exporters and importers, tracking US-Europe flows.

title: GRI, Bangladesh’s BGMEA sign pact to boost sustainability transparency
summary:
Amsterdam-based Global Reporting Initiative and the Bangladesh trade body BGMEA have signed a strategic partnership agreement to advance the Improving Transparency for Sustainable Business (ITSB) initiative in the country’s textile and apparel sector. 
BGMEA will offer sectoral leadership to advance a shared vision for transparent, responsible and sustainable business practices in the sector.

title: EU slowdown deepens Bangladesh apparel industry concerns
summary:
Bangladesh’s apparel exports to the EU reportedly fell 18.89 per cent year-on-year in January-May 2026, the steepest drop among major suppliers.
The fall outpaced declines for China, India and Vietnam, signalling pressure beyond weak demand and lower prices.
Exporters face urgency to reduce reliance on the EU and US and move into higher-value and technical products.

title: Japan’s apparel imports reach $11.7 bn in first half of 2026
summary:
Japan’s textile trade remained resilient in H1 2026, with apparel imports rising 6.0 per cent and textile yarn and fabric imports increasing 8.1 per cent, signalling firm consumer demand and manufacturing activity.
June recorded even stronger growth across imports and exports, while textile machinery exports outpaced other segments, reflecting sustained investment in production capability.

title: Can Bangladesh protect jobs while embracing AI and automation?
summary:
AI and automation could eliminate 1.22 million jobs in Bangladesh’s apparel sector by 2041, with women facing the greatest risk, as per a new study. 
While smart manufacturing promises higher productivity and competitiveness, experts say only rapid reskilling and policy reforms can prevent technology from becoming a major employment crisis.

title: US’ Deckers Brands crosses $1 bn Q1 revenue as HOKA, UGG grow
summary:
Deckers Brands reported Q1 FY27 revenue of $1.02 billion, up 5.7 per cent, driven by HOKA and UGG brand growth. 
HOKA sales rose 7.7 per cent to $703.5 million, while UGG increased 4.9 per cent to $278 million. 
DTC sales grew 13 per cent, and the company raised FY27 EPS guidance to $7.35-$7.50 while maintaining revenue outlook of $5.86-5.91 billion.

title: The net-tariff ledger: Who actually pays more on July 24
summary:
From July 24, the US 10 per cent import surcharge expires as a new forced-labour duty takes effect across 60 economies.
Caps mean most mainstream apparel from the EU, Taiwan, Japan, South Korea and Switzerland avoids added duty where base rates exceed ceilings.
China and 37 other economies face a 2.5-point increase, affecting landed-cost planning for sourcing teams.

title: Bangladesh labour reforms gain ILO backing amid LDC transition
summary:
ILO chief Gilbert F Houngbo held high-level talks in Bangladesh on labour law reform, social dialogue, job creation and social protection.
The agenda matters for apparel exporters and factory operators tracking compliance in the ready-made garment sector.
Bangladesh’s labour complaint is set to return to the ILO Governing Body in March 2027.

title: Bangladesh doubles ERQ for goods, exporters relying heavily on imports
summary:
Bangladesh Bank has doubled the exporters' retention quota for goods, exporters relying heavily on imported raw materials, intermediate goods, machinery and other production inputs, raising the permissible retention limit from 7.5 per cent to 15 per cent of the repatriated FOB value. 
The decision is expected to provide exporters with greater flexibility in managing their foreign currency requirements.

title: Bulgaria's apparel exports extend fourth year of decline
summary:
Bulgaria's apparel exports fell 19.9 per cent year on year to $254.56 million in Q1 2026, extending a multi-year decline from the 2022 peak amid weaker European demand and shifting sourcing patterns.
Germany remained the largest export market, followed by France and Italy.
Cotton apparel dominated exports, while trousers and shorts remained the country's leading apparel export category.

title: Is China+1 dead? How FTAs give India a second chance
summary:
Chief mentor of CMAI, Rahul Mehta said India captured only limited gains from the China+1 sourcing shift as buyers sought greater scale, while Bangladesh and Vietnam advanced faster. 
With apparel exports at $16.29 billion last year and $4.19 billion in Q1 2026, FTAs offer fresh opportunities, but compliance, labour, quality and scale remain key hurdles.

title: US apparel importers face brief tariff window before section 301
summary:
US apparel importers may see a roughly 48-hour tariff gap as the 10 per cent Section 122 surcharge is scheduled to expire on July 24, 2026.
A proposed Section 301 duty of 10 per cent or 12.5 per cent on imports from 60 economies has not yet been finalised.
Customs-entry timing will be critical for landed-cost planning and shipment release.
